# U.S. and Iran Blow Through Deadline to Agree to a Broad Deal to End War

President Trump said a cease-fire agreed in June would lead to limits on Iran’s nuclear program and finish the conflict, but the countries appear far apart.

![People walk and stand on a paved area next to a wall with a colorful mural. Golden minarets are visible above trees in the background.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/08/17/multimedia/17int-iran-mou-hfo-1-klhg/17int-iran-mou-hfo-1-klhg-articleLarge.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&disable=upscale)
![Aaron Boxerman](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2023/09/22/reader-center/author-aaron-boxerman/author-aaron-boxerman-thumbLarge.png "Aaron Boxerman")

By [Aaron Boxerman](https://www.nytimes.com/by/aaron-boxerman)

Reporting from Tel Aviv

The United States and Iran on Monday missed their 60-day deadline to reach a deal to curtail Iran’s nuclear program under the terms of the cease-fire they agreed to in June, underlining the breakdown of a truce that President Trump promised would end the war.

Mr. Trump had announced the so-called [memorandum of understanding](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/25/us/politics/trump-iran-cease-fire-collapse.html) between the two countries with great fanfare two months ago. # Trump threatens to bomb Oman if it 'gets in the way' over Iran issue

![](https://static.files.bbci.co.uk/bbcdotcom/web/20260729-174851-148577b706-web-3.17.0-2/grey-placeholder.png)
![Getty Images A close up shot of President Donald Trump speaking to outside with his hand raised. He is wearing a "make America great again" cap](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/9cbd/live/ce084930-9a40-11f1-a86b-519b4d19bbee.jpg.webp)

President Donald Trump has threatened to bomb Oman if it "gets in the way" of the US's own talks with Iran, Fox News reports.

A reporter for the network said the US president made the comment during a phone call on Monday, during which he also said the US had a direct backchannel with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

The IRGC later denied it was involved in talks with the US. But Iranian officials said on Monday they were close to finalising with Iran a deal on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Meanwhile, the 60-day Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) ends on Monday. The memo was a signed commitment from both the US and Iran for further talks to reach a final agreement.

Oman, which says it is a neutral country in this conflict, has suffered a number of strikes from Iran since the conflict broke out. However, it is now playing a role in negotiating with Iran to reopen the strait.

# The Strait of Hormuz: Persistent U.S.-Iran maritime flashpoint

Trump’s war on Iran has placed the narrow and congested waterway in the middle of the battlefield, driving a spike in oil and gas prices worldwide.

# Europe Cut Its Russian Gas Dependence. Now Russia Is Targeting the Alternatives in Africa

![Europe Cut Its Russian Gas Dependence. Now Russia Is Targeting the Alternatives in Africa](https://storage.united24media.com/thumbs/1920x/a/4f/bb28d51654a62e84b230a4482df034fa.png "Europe Cut Its Russian Gas Dependence. Now Russia Is Targeting the Alternatives in Africa")

Europe has largely achieved what once seemed impossible: reducing Russia’s share of EU gas imports from 45% to 13%. But diversification alone has not solved the problem of energy security. Europe’s search for new suppliers increasingly leads to Africa, where Russia is systematically trying to make precisely this alternative unviable.

![Google logo](https://united24media.com/static/build/img/google.DR7xrSi5.svg)
![Photo of Aliona Chudnovets]( "Photo of Aliona Chudnovets")

Gas is critical for heat production and the EU’s second-largest [source](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/interactive-publications/energy-2026) of electricity. Unlike oil, which is traded on a single global market and can therefore be purchased from another supplier if one stops deliveries, albeit at a higher price, a disruption in gas supplies creates an immediate crisis.

The impact of cutting off gas is disproportionate to the revenue the supplier loses. Before the war, the EU [imported](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/infographics/where-does-the-eu-s-g

# [Ukrainian Strikes Halt Most Russian Grain Export Capacity in Black Sea Region](https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/08/17/ukrainian-strikes-halt-most-russian-grain-export-capacity-in-black-sea-region-a93517)

## 

![](https://static.themoscowtimes.com/img/flipboard_mrrw.png)
![](https://static.themoscowtimes.com/image/article_1360/96/2026-07-28T162457Z_745772473_RC2JDMA1TPE7_RTRMADP_3_UKRAINE-CRISIS-RUSSIA-GRAIN.jpg)

More than 90% of Russia’s grain export capacity in the Azov-Black Sea basin has been taken offline following Ukrainian attacks and navigation restrictions, disrupting the country’s main export corridor during the busiest part of the season.

All three grain terminals at the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk suspended operations last week. Together, the terminals had handled around 25 million metric tons of Russian grain exports.

Navigation in the Sea of Azov has been suspended since July, while a grain terminal at Taman halted operations in late July. Two terminals in Novorossiysk — NKHP and NZT — stopped operating on the same day last week, followed a day later by KSK, the port’s largest terminal.

Tuapse, the smallest of Russia’s deep-water grain terminals, is the only port in the region still operating, according to Andrei Sizov, managing director of the SovEcon agricultural consultancy.
